articles.headline: Barcelona boss Hansi Flick on Lamine Yamal: 'Easier' to substitute when he scores
articles.description: Hansi Flick said it's easier to substitute Lamine Yamal when he's scored after the forward starred in Saturday's 6-1 LaLiga win over Alavés at Spotify Camp Nou.
articles.headlineJa: バルセロナのハンジ・フリック監督、ラミン・ヤマルについて：「彼がゴールを決めれば、交代させやすい」
articles.descriptionJa: 土曜日にスポティファイ・カンプ・ノウで行われたラ・リーガのアラベス戦（6-1で勝利）で活躍したラミン・ヤマルについて、ハンジ・フリック監督は、彼がゴールを決めた後であれば交代させるのも容易だと語った。
articles.body:
Hansi Flick said it's easier to substitute Lamine Yamal when he's scored after the forward starred in Saturday's 6-1 LaLiga win over Alavés at Spotify Camp Nou.

Yamal netted a brace as Barça returned to winning ways after back-to-back defeats to Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid.

The teenager has now started all 18 games for Barça and Spain this season, although he was afforded a short rest against Alavés, with Flick able to take him off for the final 20 minutes with the game won.

"When you score two goals, it's easier to go out," Flick said after substituting Yamal for just the fourth time this season.

"I spoke with him at half time [about managing his minutes]. For us, that he has the confidence back with the one vs. one situations, more time and minutes in the second half [is good], but it also important he has less minutes."

Barça opened the scoring early on through Raphinha before Fermín López added the second in the 23rd minute.

Raphinha's second of the game, and his 17th of the season, made it 3-0 and Yamal capped a fine team move with a brilliant finish from the edge of the box to make it four by half time.

Yamal netted another after the break, a dinked finish over the goalkeeper initially ruled out for offside, and Anthony Gordon scored the sixth late on prior to an even later consolation goal from Mariano Díaz.

It was just what Barça needed after a week which saw their 11-game winning run halted by losses to PSG in the Champions League and Madrid in the league.

"For Lamine it was a great game, but it was good to see the level of the attack: Fermín, Rapha," Flick added.

"This is what I want to see after these two defeats. How we react, it was good and in the right way."

Flick also had praise for his makeshift defence, with midfielder Frenkie de Jong featuring at centre-back and youngster Brian Fariñas, also a midfielder, making his full debut at right-back.

"At the moment we have to think different," Flick said. "Four defenders are out in Xavi Espart, Andreas [Christensen], Jules [Koundé] and Eric Garcìa.

"Hopefully some will come back, but we don't know when yet. So I asked Frenkie if he's able to play there; he said 'Yes, when I can help the team I will do it.'

"The same with Brian. I don't know if he ever played [at right-back], maybe in La Masia, but he also played a good level.

"I am happy for him. He deserved these minutes, this game. He is focused, top in training, very professional. This is what we want from him and the players."

- Gordon, Yamal, Raphinha on target as Barcelona hit Alavés for six

Fariñas, 20, looked especially comfortable playing on the same flank as Yamal, someone he played with at youth level.

"You could see he is connected with Lamine," Flick continued. "It's very important. He helped us a lot today playing this position."

The win took Barça back to the top of the table after Atlético Madrid had leapfrogged them earlier on Saturday.

articles.headline: Derwin James placed on injured reserve after hamstring rehab setback
articles.description: The Chargers have placed safety Derwin James Jr. on injured reserve because of a hamstring injury.
articles.headlineJa: ダーウィン・ジェームズ、ハムストリングのリハビリで挫折し故障者リスト入り
articles.descriptionJa: チャージャーズは、ハムストリングの負傷により、セーフティのダーウィン・ジェームズ・ジュニアを故障者リスト（IR）に登録した。
articles.body:
EL SEGUNDO, Calif. -- The Los Angeles Chargers placed safety Derwin James Jr. on injured reserve with a hamstring injury on Saturday.

The Pro Bowl safety hasn't played since a loss at Buffalo on Sept. 27. The move wasn't unexpected after coach Jim Harbaugh said this week that James suffered a setback in his rehab and recovery.

James will have to sit out a minimum of four games for the Chargers (0-6), who face the Los Angeles Rams (3-4) on Sunday.

The Chargers signed cornerback Isas Waxter to the active roster and promoted cornerback Kaiir Elam from the practice squad.

In addition to James, left guard Kayode Awosika will miss a fifth straight game because of a leg injury. Defensive back Deane Leonard (concussion) and wide receiver Brenen Thompson (quad/hamstring) also were ruled out.

Waxter spent last season on the Bolts' practice squad after initially signing as an undrafted free agent with Seattle. He has appeared in a pair of games this season as a standard elevation.

Elam has started 19 of 43 career regular-season games with Buffalo, Dallas and Tennessee.

articles.headline: Zach Charbonnet, Jadarian Price have no game designations for Monday
articles.description: Seahawks running backs Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price have no game designations, meaning both are healthy enough to play Monday night against the Bears.
articles.body:
RENTON, Wash. -- Seattle Seahawks running backs Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price have no game designations, meaning both are healthy enough to play Monday night against the Chicago Bears at Lumen Field.

Coach Mike Macdonald confirmed that Charbonnet will make his 2026 debut, but he stopped short of declaring that Seattle will activate Price off injured reserve this week.

The Seahawks ruled out two starters in left tackle Charles Cross (ankle) and wide receiver/kick returner Rashid Shaheed (knee), as well as backup running back Velus Jones Jr. (hamstring). Starting outside linebacker Uchenna Nwosu (ankle) is doubtful.

Price, Seattle's rookie first-round pick, has missed the last four games with a chest injury. He was limited in his return to practice Thursday, then was a full participant the last two days. Price does not have to be activated until Monday to play against Chicago. That would require the Seahawks to clear a spot on their 53-man roster.

"We'll see if that's what we do," Macdonald said. "We've got some things going on rosterwise that we're working through right now, but we have a plan for Zach."

Asked whether Price might not play due to a reason unrelated to his health, Macdonald said, "We're just going to let the transaction speak for itself on that one."

Emanuel Wilson and George Holani have led Seattle's backfield with Price on IR and Charbonnet working his way back from the torn left ACL he suffered in the divisional round of the playoffs on Jan. 17. He told reporters last week that he had surgery on Feb. 12, meaning he's not yet nine months removed from the operation.

The Seahawks activated Charbonnet off the physically unable to perform list on Oct. 22, which was the deadline to do so as he had returned to practice 21 days earlier. He was inactive last Sunday night against the Kansas City Chiefs after full participation in all three practices that week.

The Seahawks listed Charbonnet as a full participant Thursday and Saturday of this week and limited Friday.

"To come back on the timetable that he has and to be in the position that he is, and the work ethic that he's shown and being able to work through what it takes to get back from an injury like that at this point in time is remarkable," Macdonald said. "Zach's a guy that kind of works in the shadows. He's already had our respect, but hopefully people understand what kind of stud this guy is to come back on this timetable and be ready to go."

Cross, Shaheed and Jones all left the Chiefs game and were unable to return. None practiced this week. Nwosu also did not practice this week.

A source told the NFL Network's Ian Rapoport that Cross has a high ankle sprain that could sideline him for one or two games.

Macdonald said of Shaheed, who also returns kickoffs and punts: "He's doing well. He just wasn't able to make it to the game obviously, and we'll see next week. But he's done a great job."

articles.headline: Victor Wembanyama's Halloween costume trend returns with 'The Witcher' look
articles.description: With a game on Halloween, the San Antonio Spurs center's costume trend returned in spectacular fashion.
articles.body:
SAN ANTONIO -- San Antonio Spurs star Victor Wembanyama resumed his custom of donning viral Halloween fits by showing up Saturday at Frost Bank Center dressed as Geralt of Rivia from his favorite book series "The Witcher."

"Why is it my favorite? Because it feels as much like a fantasy book, epic fantasy, as a dive into human psychology, and emotions," Wembanyama said. "The characters are so deep. After reading seven books, it's like I know these characters like they're friends or family members. It's a great, great series. My favorite."

In the series, Geralt of Rivia serves as the protagonist, a solitary hunter who travels and makes a living taking down monsters in a world where humans often prove to be more diabolical than the beasts he's chasing.

The 22-year old had temporarily paused his Halloween ritual last season because the Spurs didn't play a game on the holiday.

"We don't got a game on Halloween," he said last year. "So, we don't get to see a costume this year, unfortunately."

Clearly, Wembanyama was making up for lost time with this latest fit.

The last time Wembanyama arrived at an NBA arena in a costume for Halloween was 2024, when the Frenchman dressed as No-Face, a character from the Academy-Award winning animated film "Spirited Away." Wembanyama sported an all-black one-piece outfit and wore the character's trademark mask.

That night he dropped 25 points at the Delta Center in Utah with nine rebounds, seven assists, five steals and five blocks, marking the second time in his career he tallied at least five each in five statistical categories in a 106-88 win over the Jazz.

Wembanyama started his Halloween tradition in 2023 as a rookie, arriving at Mortgage Matchup Center in Phoenix rocking a costume derived from the fictional supernatural creature Slenderman. Wembanyama racked up 18 points, eight rebounds, and four blocks later that night in a 115-114 victory over the Suns.

This Halloween marked Wembanyama's first time playing at his home arena, and a few of his teammates joined in on the fun. Point guard De'Aaron Fox and his family dressed as characters from the Disney film "Toy Story" while Keldon Johnson maintained his Halloween tradition of dressing like a cowboy for the holiday.

The day before Halloween, backup center Luke Kornet remained undecided about whether to dress up for the holiday.

"I might be wearing a costume," Kornet said. "If I am, I'm going to be Captain [Georg] von Trapp from "The Sound of Music" because my children love it and we listen to the soundtrack a ton. I still need to find his little whistle. I can just wear a suit, basically, right? I don't really invest too much into my outfits, but I want the whistle."

articles.headline: Anthony Gordon, Lamine Yamal, Raphinha on target as Barcelona hit Alavés for six
articles.description: Free-scoring Barcelona put six past Alavés as they bounced back from defeat against Real Madrid in style.
articles.body:
Free-scoring Barcelona put six past Alavés as they bounced back from defeat against Real Madrid in style.

A 2-1 loss to their rivals last time out represented their first dropped points of the season but it was back to business as usual as the table toppers thumped their visitors 6-1 at the Nou Camp.

There were two goals apiece for Raphinha and Lamine Yamal, as well as one from Fermín López and a late topper from England's Anthony Gordon coming off the bench. Mariano Díaz grabbed the late consolation for the Basque outfit.

Hansi Flick was without a handful of first-teamers, including Jules Koundé, Eric García, Andreas Christensen, Dani Olmo, Roony Bardghji, and Xavi Espart, but their collective absence was barely noticed as they made an emphatic start.

Lopez was straight into his work, driving through the defensive line and laying on a simple chance for Raphinha to slot home after just eight minutes.

Abde Rebbach was off target when he had an early opportunity to return fire and the gulf in quality showed when Lopez doubled the lead with a fiery finish. Cutting into the penalty area on the right he read a pass from Yamal then rifled powerfully across Antonio Sivera from a tight angle.

There were already signs of damage limitation by the time Sivera made a wonderful save from Yamal but that merely delayed further pain. Lopez once again found himself at the heart of things, sniping possession in midfield and unleashing Raphinha with a beautifully weighted pass.

The Brazilian let the ball run to the edge of the area then unleashed a precision left-foot finish. With seconds to go before the half-time whistle, the hosts showcased their dominance again, stroking a long sequence of passes in the final third before Yamal pulled the trigger with a bullet of a first-time finish.

With an hour gone and the urgency abating, Gabriel Jesus entered the fray and laid on Barca's fifth with a neat touch. Yamal's delicate flicked finish was initially chalked off for offside flag, but replays overruled the flag.

Barca were not satisfied yet, rounding out their night's work through another of Flick's replacements. Gordon was the beneficiary of a defence-splitting ball from Rodri, with the former Newcastle winger charging down on goal then lifting his shot calmly over the keeper for his first league goal.

But the last word went to a former Real man, with Diaz taking advantage of some slack defending in stoppage time as he went clear and caught Joan García flat-footed.

articles.headline: Christian Pulisic scores as AC Milan beat rivals Inter Milan
articles.description: Christian Pulisic scored inside five minutes while Diego Moreira scored and added two assists as AC Milan beat rivals Inter 3-1.
articles.body:
Christian Pulisic scored inside five minutes while Diego Moreira scored and added two assists as AC Milan snapped Inter Milan's nine-match unbeaten run this Serie A season in a 3-1 victory at San Siro.

United States star Pulisic was once again a thorn in Inter's side, connecting with Moreira's delivery in the fourth minute of the Derby della Madonnina to open the scoring.

Moreira's corner then perfectly set up Adrien Rabiot for the hosts' second, before Alessandro Bastoni clawed a goal back in the 22nd minute.

Moreira added his own name to the list of goal-scorers in the 43rd minute, ultimately consigning Inter to defeat, anointing Lazio new league leaders, and extending their own unbeaten run in the derby to five matches.

It was determined work from Moreira to set up the opener, calmly controlling the ball as he worked his way down the right before issuing an excellent cross for Pulisic, who nodded it home.

Rabiot doubled the lead in the 10th minute from Moreira's creatively worked corner, taking the visitors and Josep Martínez by surprise when he directed it in off the far post.

Inter finally had a chance through Carlos Augusto, who was off-target, before Bastoni cut the deficit in half.

It came from a Hakan Çalhanoglu corner, flicked on by Manuel Akanji, before Bastoni nodded into the bottom corner at the near post.

Calhanoglu then tried himself, forcing Mike Maignan to tip his effort over the crossbar, and the French keeper reacted quickly to keep out Marcus Thuram's header from a corner.

Momentum had shifted in Inter's favour following the Bastoni goal, and it required a brilliant, lightning-quick reaction from Maignan to deny Djed Spence from point-blank range.

Moreira extended the hosts' advantage with two minutes remaining in stoppage time from a free-kick.

It looked as though there was some debate as to whether he or Pulisic might take it, but their decision proved the correct one when the Belgian floated it over the wall with his left foot, giving Martinez no chance.

Andy Diouf attempted to reduce the deficit with a lob 10 minutes into the second half, and there was a chance from a great Calhanoglu delivery for Augusto, who chose to head it but directed it wide.

Strahinja Pavlovic played a critical part in preserving the hosts' lead with a timely tackle, then kept the pressure on Marcus Thuram, who could only direct an effort straight at Maignan.

Inter briefly had hope of a penalty for a handball, but it was correctly overturned after VAR confirmed the ball had struck Mario Gila's midsection.

Substitute Alphadjo Cissè nearly made it four in stoppage time, but a good stop by Martinez to tip it over prevented any further damage.

articles.headline: Fantasy football last-minute pickups: Geno Smith, Ryan Flournoy are top options
articles.description: If injuries, bye weeks or tough matchups have you seeking lineup help, Matt Bowen lists potential options.
articles.body:
At various points during the fantasy football season, injuries, bye weeks and breaking news can cause you to need reinforcements for your fantasy lineup. Every Friday throughout the 2026 NFL season, Matt Bowen will offer some late-week pickup options at each of the primary fantasy positions to help fill those holes, with an emphasis on deeper leagues.

Because of that, this column will focus mostly on players rostered in under 50% of ESPN leagues, with occasional exceptions.

This week, we will start with a veteran passer in a positive matchup and a dual-threat option who is coming off a season-best performance in Week 7. At wide receiver, I see two options with higher floors given their route tree and anticipated usage, plus I have an upside play, too. As usual, the running back spot is pretty lean, but there are some deeper-league targets. And we'll finish with a tight end seeing consistent volume and take a shot at a D/ST in a tough week to find quality matchups.

Quarterbacks

Geno Smith, New York Jets (25.4% rostered; vs. Raiders)

Smith had 23.48 fantasy points last week against Miami (his second-highest total of the season) and he was really efficient with the ball, completing 76.7% of his throws. Smith finished with 287 yards and three touchdowns, plus the emergence of rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. -- two straight games of 100 or more yards receiving -- gives the Jets a rising playmaker. On Sunday, it's a matchup with a Raiders defense ranking in the bottom five against quarterbacks, so let's get Smith in the lineup as a fringe QB1.

Malik Willis, Miami Dolphins (9.1% rostered; at Patriots) 

Willis had a season-best 26.02 points against the Jets in Week 7, and while the passing numbers don't jump here, Willis did throw two touchdown passes in that game, and he brings a dual-threat element to the lineup. Willis has at least 37 yards rushing, eight carries and a touchdown in back-to-back games, and he finished with 74 yards on the ground in Week 5 versus the Bengals. He can be played as a superflex starter this week against the Patriots.

Wide receivers

Ryan Flournoy, Dallas Cowboys (19.3% rostered; vs, Cardinals)

Flournoy has had double-digit fantasy points in three straight games. He has established himself as Dak Prescott's No. 3 option behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, so he provides a stable floor as a deeper-league target for Sunday's matchup versus the Cardinals.

Antonio Williams, Washington Commanders (13.5% rostered; vs. Eagles)

With Terry McLaurin (knee) out for the season, there is real opportunity here for Williams. The rookie is a savvy route runner, one who can find and settle in open space. Williams is scoring 7.4 fantasy PPG, but with increased usage, his numbers can rise as a middle-of-the-field option/outlet for Jayden Daniels.

articles.headline: Avdija scores 24 and Lillard has 22 as Portland rolls over Utah 112-90
articles.description: — Deni Avdija scored 24 points, Damian Lillard added 22, and the Portland Trail Blazers rebounded from their first loss of the season by blowing past the Utah Jazz 112-90 on Saturday.
articles.body:
SALT LAKE CITY -- — Deni Avdija scored 24 points, Damian Lillard added 22, and the Portland Trail Blazers rebounded from their first loss of the season by blowing past the Utah Jazz 112-90 on Saturday.


              Toumani Camara, Scoot Henderson, and Jrue Holiday each tallied 14 points as Portland (4-1) rebounded from losing to Memphis on Thursday.


              Rookie Darryn Peterson scored 16 points and Lauri Markkanen had 13 points on 3-for-14 shooting for the Jazz in their fourth straight loss.


              The game marked the first time Utah hasn't reached 103 points this season with the Blazers forcing Utah's lowest shooting percentage of the season at 37.1%. 


              The Jazz have been hampered by turnovers throughout the early season (20 in this game) and Portland's defense took advantage, forcing four straight turnovers during one stretch in the third quarter.


              In just one half, Avdija went 10 for 11 from the line and had 19 points, sparking the Blazers to a 59-42 lead at halftime. Utah never challenged in the second half and the Blazers led by 26 in the third quarter.


              The Blazers held Utah scoreless for nearly six minutes in the opening quarter during a 17-0 run. Holiday's free throws gave Portland a 23-7 lead with 3:29 left in the first period.


              The Jazz welcomed Markkanen back after he missed two games with a sprained wrist, but he and Keyonte George combined to miss their first nine shots as the Blazers sprinted to their early lead. George, Utah's leading scorer with a 24.4 average, finished with eight points.


              The Blazers were thin in the backcourt without Ja Morant, who strained his hamstring against Memphis and won't be back before Thanksgiving, and Shaedon Sharpe, who is out until the spring after knee surgery. But Portland cruised with tight defense and 48-37 rebounding edge.


              Up next
              Blazers: Visit the Denver Nuggets on Monday night.


              Jazz: Visit the San Antonion Spurs on Monday night.

articles.headline: T'Vondre Sweat placed on injured reserve with knee injury
articles.description: The Jets will be without T'Vondre Sweat for at least the next four games, as the starting nose tackle was placed on injured reserve Saturday with a knee sprain.
articles.headlineJa: T'Vondre Sweat、膝の負傷により負傷者リスト入り
articles.descriptionJa: ジェッツは、スターティング・ノーズタックルのT'Vondre Sweatを欠くことになる。土曜日に膝の捻挫により負傷者リストに登録されたため、少なくとも今後4試合は欠場する見込みだ。
articles.body:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- The New York Jets will be without T'Vondre Sweat for at least the next four games, as the starting nose tackle was placed on injured reserve Saturday with a knee sprain.

The good news for Sweat is that it's not considered a season-ending injury, a source said. The 366-pound run stuffer will be eligible to return Nov. 29 against the Miami Dolphins.

Sweat already had been ruled out for Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders (3-4) at MetLife Stadium. His injury, which occurred last Sunday, comes at an inopportune time for the Jets, who have been struggling to stop the run. They're allowing 127.7 yards per game, 24th in the NFL.

Rookie Darrell Jackson Jr., a fourth-round pick from Florida State, is expected to replace Sweat in the lineup.

The Jets (2-5), losers of two straight, don't expect to have rookie edge rusher David Bailey (groin), who is doubtful for the game. To replace Sweat and Bailey on the game-day roster, they brought up Payton Page (signed to the roster) and Quinton Bell (elevation) from the practice squad, respectively.

The Jets are thin at defensive tackle. They're already down David Onyemata (core muscle surgery), who was placed on IR in Week 3.

Sweat was acquired in an offseason trade with the Tennessee Titans. After missing a chunk of training camp with a hamstring injury, he has appeared in all seven games, with no sacks, two tackles-for-loss and 17 total tackles.

articles.headline: Lakers' Jeanie Buss accuses siblings of 'cloak and dagger' tactics
articles.description: Jeanie Buss accused her siblings of conspiring against her in court filings responding to her siblings' ongoing effort to sell their shares in the Lakers.
articles.headlineJa: レイカーズのジーニー・バス、兄弟らの「隠密な」策動を非難
articles.descriptionJa: ジーニー・バスは、レイカーズの株式売却を進める兄弟らに対し、自身に対して共謀していると法廷文書で非難した。
articles.body:
In a court filing this week, Jeanie Buss accused her siblings of conspiring against her in a "cloak and dagger" campaign through the media, said they were jealous that their father picked her over them to govern the Los Angeles Lakers and asked a judge to block her siblings' attempt to sell the family's shares in the team, which would end her run as the Lakers' governor.

Wednesday's filing, reviewed by ESPN, is the latest salvo in the bitter legal battle playing out between Jeanie and her siblings, namely Joey and Jesse Buss, leading up to a scheduled Dec. 8 hearing in Los Angeles Superior Court.

The filing responds to recent filings by Jeanie's siblings, who are seeking to sell the family's remaining shares of the Lakers to the Bob Iger and Josh Kushner ownership group, who are seeking to buy the team from Mark Walter at a $12.5 billion valuation.

"The conflicts that ensued after Dr. [Jerry] Buss's death [in 2013] were sadly inevitable, and no doubt intensified given that Dr. Buss chose his daughter over four sons to be his successor," Jeanie's lawyers wrote in the Wednesday filing.

"Respondents' obsession with tearing down Jeanie and their inability to accept that she would be a part of the Lakers' future is borne of this classic succession parable."

In 2025, Walter bought a majority stake in the Lakers from the Buss family at a $10 billion valuation. During that sale, the Buss family retained a 17.82% stake, just above the NBA's 15% minimum for the family to retain control. The family also received go-along rights. On Aug. 17, ESPN's Shams Charania reported that Johnny, Jim, Janie, Joey and Jesse Buss had voted to sell the remaining family shares to Iger and Kushner using those go-along rights.

Each sibling stands to make an additional $371 million if the family sells the entirety of its shares via the go-along provision.

Jeanie has attempted to block those attempts to sell, saying that her siblings must obey a 2017 court order that required the two co-trustees, Janie and Joey, to always vote to ensure she remained the controlling owner of the team.

In Wednesday's filing, she again asked the court to remove Joey and Janie as co-trustees of the trust for breach of fiduciary duty, to hold them in contempt of court, to find Jim, Johnny and Jesse liable for aiding and abetting a violation of the 2017 court order, and for her to be reimbursed for legal costs.

Sources close to the family have told ESPN that there have been settlement talks between the two sides, but it's unclear how much progress has been made leading up to the scheduled December hearing.

"Jeanie had no choice but to seek court intervention to enforce the clear terms of the trust and this court's 2017 order," Wednesday's filing states. "Respondents respond [by] casting themselves as victims, when in reality, the entire episode is their own false flag operation.
